sources.title: Czech Archaeological Atlas: Šárka hillfort
sources.note: Site description: probable eighth-century beginnings, tenth-century abandonment, elite contacts and rise of Přemyslid centres. Public identity is regional, not a claim of one state throughout 700 to 900.

sources.title: Martin Kuna and colleagues, Archaeological Atlas of Bohemia: Březno
sources.note: Printed pages 71 to 72. Eighth-century houses followed by ninth-century variety; 1984 experiment with family of five for thirteen days; separate winter smoke experiments. Original indexed pages checked; direct large PDF fetch failed. Combined passages kept under 200 words.

sources.title: Naďa Profantová and colleagues: Tismice as a production and regional centre
sources.note: 2020 primary article abstract: final third of eighth century through ninth, approximately 170 metal ornaments, workshop ingots and blanks, gold work found in 2018. No date attached to every individual object.

sources.title: Czech Archaeological Atlas: Doubravčice
sources.note: Eighth-century reuse of older enclosure; distinction between prehistoric/early medieval ramparts and later field boundaries.

sources.title: Czech Archaeological Atlas: Levý Hradec
sources.note: Settlement around mid-ninth century, successive fortification, Bořivoj and church in 880s.

sources.title: Czech Archaeological Atlas: Budeč
sources.note: Foundation final third of ninth or early tenth century; stone-faced timber-earth wall, palisaded residence, surviving rotunda. Date straddles mapped end and is labelled.

sources.title: Prague Castle Administration: Archaeological research
sources.note: Sites of archaeological excavations: Church of Virgin Mary, late ninth century; preserved masonry, marly limestone floor tiles and altar. Do not project later water pipes into early phase.

sources.title: Jiří Militký and Naďa Profantová: Roman coins and a denier of Charlemagne from Tismice
sources.note: Numismatický sborník 27/2, printed 181, catalogue no. 3: Amiens denier 771 to 793/794; obverse CARO / LVS. Printed 182 to 183 interpretation of mint. Coin found 2011, not 2012 Roman finds. Imported Latin, not written Czech.

sources.title: Lumír Poláček: Great Moravia and the power centre at Mikulčice
sources.note: Printed pages 19 to 21: early landscape, eighth-century core, hooked spurs and Avar bronzes, subsequent ninth-century expansion. Pages 32 to 33: burial change around 800 not simply proof of Christianisation. Public excerpts selected carefully to keep combined derivation under 200 words.

sources.title: Zdeněk Měřínský: Production, crafts and trade before and during Great Moravia
sources.note: Printed page 115 in Great Moravia and the Beginnings of Christianity: pre-Great Moravian bone/antler waste, needle cases, clothing tools, woodworking. Indexed original full page checked. Ambiguous bone skates and later luxury craft excluded. Same work as arub.cz mirror, count as one source.

sources.title: Hana Marešová: Early medieval iron production in the Uničov area
sources.note: 2014 primary research abstract: three Dolní Sukolom furnaces dated by analogy to eighth/ninth-century turn; underground form with long tunnel; slag/ore analysis. Brníčko is eleventh/twelfth-century and excluded. Root verified original PDF printed page 3, author Hana Marešová, three furnaces, analogy dating and shared ore chemistry: https://archeologia-technica.cz/media/AT_25_2014_03-17_Maresova.pdf

sources.title: Jiří Macháček: The Rise of Medieval Towns and States in East Central Europe
sources.note: 2010 Brill monograph, printed page 113: Forest Nursery pre-Great Moravian phases, pottery and cremation urns, earlier houses overlain by later fortification. Original book indexed text checked; direct fetch failed.

sources.title: Zuzana Hofmanová and colleagues: Ancient genomes and early medieval Moravia
sources.note: 2025 primary research, sampling context: Pohansko-Severovýchodní Předhradí newborn burial H205/PJP010 dated seventh/eighth centuries. Used only for child/context, no national/genetic identity inference.

sources.title: Jiří Macháček and colleagues: Runes from Lány
sources.note: Journal of Archaeological Science 127 (2021), 105333, results text alongside Figure 5 and discussion. Bone around 600, earlier than mapped 700 to 800. First two runes incomplete; quote only intact final four ᛖᛗᛞᛟ, e m d o. Alphabet exercise, not translatable sentence. Primary PDF indexed full page checked; direct tool returns empty page.

sources.title: Jiří Macháček: Knowledge transmission and the inception of literacy in Central Europe
sources.note: 2024 primary scholarly discussion, Glagolitic Script section: introduction in ninth-century Great Moravia and Carolingian Pannonia. Earlier rune interpretation remains cautious.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Imported 700 to 900, Bohemian footprint 12.400 to 16.684 E and 48.719 to 50.908 N. Distinct from later Bohemia and Czech Republic cards. Budeč chronology explicitly crosses 900. Writing is contemporary imported Latin on an actual Tismice object, not invented Czech.

Imported 700 to 800, bbox 15.712 to 19.417 E and 47.952 to 50.190 N. Regional cultural label distinct from existing Great Moravia card. Lány around 600 explicitly earlier; Dolní Sukolom around 800 crosses boundary; ninth-century Glagolitic explicitly later. No modern nation substitution or automatic successor link.
